story.iWant: to detect anomalies and outliers in financial data

tasks.task: Design Anomaly data models - Define Anomaly, AnomalyDetectionResult, AnomalySeverity enum in shared/models.py
Implement detect_anomalies() function - Create raglite/insights/anomalies.py with Z-score analysis and severity classification
Add LLM-powered anomaly explanation - Implement explain_anomaly() using Mistral Large for contextual reasoning
Structured logging and context - Add logging with extra={} for anomaly metrics
Unit tests - Create tests/unit/test_anomaly_detection.py with synthetic test data
Integration tests - Create tests/integration/test_anomaly_detection_integration.py with accuracy validation
Documentation and cleanup - Add docstrings, update __init__.py, verify linting

acceptanceCriteria.ac: Anomaly detection algorithm implemented (statistical thresholds per Tech Spec) - Unit test: detect_anomalies() callable with metric and timeseries, returns List[Anomaly]
Anomalies identified: significant deviations from trends, unexpected spikes/drops, outliers - Unit test: synthetic data with known outliers correctly identified (Z-score > 2)
Anomaly severity scored (minor, moderate, critical) - Unit test: severity correctly assigned based on Z-score thresholds (|z|>3 = critical, |z|>2 = moderate)
Anomalies logged with context (metric, time period, magnitude of deviation) - Unit test: Anomaly model contains all required fields; structured logging emits context
Integration test validates anomaly detection on sample data with known outliers - Integration test: end-to-end detection on test dataset achieves 85%+ accuracy, less than 10% false positive rate

doc.title: Epic 4 PRD
doc.snippet: Anomaly detection algorithm, severity scoring (minor/moderate/critical), anomalies logged with context including metric, time period, magnitude of deviation.

doc.title: Tech Spec Epic 4
doc.snippet: Z-score analysis with threshold |z| > 2, severity levels: critical if |z| > 3 else moderate. Target 85%+ accuracy, less than 10% false positive rate. File: raglite/insights/anomalies.py (~50 lines).

doc.title: Definition of Done
doc.snippet: New code has >= 80% test coverage. All unit tests, integration tests, and E2E tests must pass. Coverage ratchet enforced by CI/CD.

doc.title: Coding Standards
doc.snippet: Type hints mandatory, Google-style docstrings, structured logging with extra={}, Pydantic models for data validation, async/await for I/O.

doc.title: Testing Strategy
doc.snippet: 80% unit tests (functions/classes), 15% integration tests (service integration), 5% E2E tests (accuracy validation).

interface.name: TimeSeriesData
interface.signature: class TimeSeriesData(BaseModel): metric_name: str, points: list[TimeSeriesPoint], interval: str, source_documents: list[str]
interface.usage: Input to detect_anomalies() function - provides time-series data for analysis

interface.name: TimeSeriesPoint
interface.signature: class TimeSeriesPoint(BaseModel): date: datetime, value: float, label: str | None
interface.usage: Individual data point within TimeSeriesData - extract value and date for Z-score calculation

interface.name: get_mistral_client
interface.usage: Get Mistral client for LLM-powered anomaly explanation. Call client.chat.complete() with explanation prompt.

interface.name: get_logger
interface.usage: Create logger for structured logging: logger.info("Anomaly detected", extra={"metric": m, "z_score": z})

tests.standards: Testing follows pytest + pytest-asyncio pattern. Unit tests mock external dependencies (Mistral client). Integration tests validate accuracy on synthetic data with known outliers. Target: 30+ tests (similar to Story 4.4 with 49 tests). Coverage: >= 80% on new code. Use @pytest.mark.asyncio for async functions. Use pytest.fixture for reusable test data. Follow test naming: test_{module}_{function}_{scenario}.py
